task: Security lens over the address-drawn population (3349cf0 vs d102712): can a crafted address inflate the child walk, allocate unboundedly or fail to terminate; is the address used only for RNG keys; is the status page still inert; did any line leak.
verdict: CONCERNS raised, then PASS after the blocking finding was fixed before the follow-up commit. One High: a crafted ?addr=v1/ hung the child walk forever. The root is shallower than GALAXY_DEPTH, so every root child read levels[1] as undefined, starKind fell back to 0 and classified them all local; the disc list never filled. Fixed twice over: generateGalaxy returns the home star alone for the root, starKind now throws on an address that is not deeper than a galaxy, and the loop is bounded at LOCAL_STAR_EVERY * (local + disc), with an assertion that the exact counts were produced. The hostile URL was then rendered end to end through the built app (capture root-url-regression, frame 42, 1/1), and normal addresses still emit 45,001 stars. Claims 1, 3, 4 and 5 confirmed; only the termination half of claim 2 was refuted, at the root.
notes: F1 (low, prospective) re-quantified now that the picture draws by address: a rich galaxy hashes 45,000 sibling keys through 32-bit FNV-1a, so ~0.24 expected colliding pairs per galaxy (~one galaxy in four draws two coincident lights under different addresses). Identity remains the Address, so this is a visual duplicate, not an identity confusion; it becomes real at the next layer arrival checks. Recorded in ticket 05 and routed to plan-architect. No secrets, credentials, absolute paths or personal data in the diff; no new network, storage or DOM sink; status.html stays static under its CSP. Cost: cents, one seat, one pass.
